Suggested Option 1: head west on I-90 to Jackson, Wyoming (approx. 18 hours), then Grand Teton and Yellowstone, Beartooth Highway to Montana, and return via I-90
Suggested Option 2: Utah's Mighty Five — Moab, Arches, Canyonlands, Capitol Reef, Bryce Canyon, and Zion, returning via I-70

The Beartooth Highway (US-212) is a 68-mile paved scenic road connecting Cooke City, Montana to Red Lodge, Montana through the Beartooth Mountains
The Beartooth Highway is generally in good condition from late May to early October, with speed limits of 45-65 mph and elevations over 10,000 feet
Advised filling up on gas in Cooke City or Red Lodge since stations are limited, and checking the Montana DOT website for closures
Colter Bay Campground is on the shores of Jackson Lake with 350 sites accommodating RVs/trailers up to 45 feet, flush toilets, showers, and potable water; reservations via recreation.gov
Colter Bay Campground has 100 sites with 30-amp electric hookups in the 'Electric Loop' section, for RVs/trailers up to 45 feet
Colter Bay Campground has a 6-month reservation window, so sites can be booked up to 6 months in advance via recreation.gov
Colter Bay Campground has several potable water stations and a free dump station near the entrance for campers
Jenny Lake Campground near Moose has 49 sites for RVs/trailers up to 30 feet with flush toilets, showers, and potable water; reservations via recreation.gov
Signal Mountain Campground on Jackson Lake has 235 sites for RVs/trailers up to 30 feet with flush toilets, showers, and potable water; reservations via recreation.gov
Granite Creek Campground in Bridger-Teton National Forest has 61 sites for RVs/trailers up to 40 feet with flush toilets, showers, and potable water
Curtis Canyon Campground in Bridger-Teton National Forest has 12 sites for RVs/trailers up to 30 feet with vault toilets and potable water
Jackson Hole Campground at Fireside Resort in Wilson, Wyoming has 200 sites for all-size RVs/trailers with flush toilets, showers, pool, and Wi-Fi
Virginian Lodge RV Resort in Jackson, Wyoming has 230 sites for all-size RVs/trailers with flush toilets, showers, pool, hot tub, and Wi-Fi
Advised reserving campsites well in advance for peak season (June to August) and bringing bear spray in both parks

Grand Teton offers scenic roads, hiking trails, and lakes; Yellowstone, America's first national park, is about 1 hour north with geysers, hot springs, wildlife, Old Faithful, and the Grand Prismatic Spring; the Beartooth Highway leg to Montana takes about 4 hours
Summer weather on the Beartooth Highway is usually mild with average highs in the 60s-70s°F (15-21°C), though occasional thunderstorms can bring heavy rain and strong winds
The Beartooth Mountains are home to bears, elk, deer, and bighorn sheep; drivers should be extra cautious at dawn and dusk when animals are most active
The Beartooth Highway reaches elevations over 10,000 feet (3,000 meters), which can cause altitude sickness; take regular breaks, stay hydrated, and watch for symptoms
Summer is peak tourist season in Yellowstone and Grand Teton National Parks, so visitors should expect crowds and long lines at popular attractions
Both Yellowstone and Grand Teton offer free shuttle services, guided tours, and ranger programs that can enhance the experience and reduce congestion
Potable water is for refilling RV tanks only, not washing vehicles; the dump station is for RV waste only; campers should conserve water and follow grey/black water disposal guidelines
Water pressure at Colter Bay's potable water stations can be high, so campers should use a pressure regulator to avoid damaging their RV's plumbing

Arches NP has over 2,000 natural arches; Canyonlands includes the Island in the Sky and The Needles districts; Bryce Canyon is known for unique hoodoos; drives between parks run 30 minutes to 2.5 hours

Yosemite features iconic landmarks like Half Dome and El Capitan; Sequoia NP has giant sequoia groves (about 4 hours from Yosemite); Kings Canyon has the deepest canyon in North America (about 1 hour further)
